thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: A fully managed drone-delivery network operating company-owned autonomous aircraft under FAA Part 135/BVLOS authority. The company positions it against this problem: Engineer perception, control and task-specific hardware around the operational workflow in logistics & warehousing. Verified current scope: multi-line/fleet/site. Stated ambition: unresolved beyond current company positioning. Public evidence supports responsibility for hardware, robot body, models/policies, integration, remote operations, ongoing support/maintenance and hardware financing/RaaS; supports only partial/shared responsibility for commissioning/qualification; does not establish responsibility for end effectors/tooling and simulation/training. Overall integration responsibility is classified as shared. Commercial evidence: 3_partner_confirmed_or_customer_pilot; technical evidence: 2_marketing_specific. These are public-evidence classifications, not proof of contract scope, uptime, economics or performance.
relevanceToIntegration: Partial integration comparator: public evidence supports a company role in integration or qualification, but responsibility is shared with a customer, OEM or partner. Commercial evidence is 3_partner_confirmed_or_customer_pilot; whole-workflow prime responsibility is not established.
